summary:
[  edit  ]
The  Primitive   SOP  is like the  Point SOP  but manipulates a  primitive 's position, size, orientation, color, alpha, in addition to primitive-specific attributes, such as reversing primitive normals. The  Primitive   SOP  also lets you create custom primitive attributes.
You can also apply parametric affine transformations to a profile by using this  SOP . You can also use it to open, close, reverse, and cycle the profile curves.
Note:  When applying transformations to a profile, you can only rotate about the Z axis because the projected curve is a planar curve that lives in the domain of the surface. Therefore it wouldn't make any sense to allow rotations in X or Y for profiles.
Transformation of Primitives vs Profiles
A Bezier surface is a single primitive, as is a NURBS surface, while a polygon mesh can consist of hundreds of individual primitives. Care must be taken to ensure the desired result. Profiles can be translated, rotated, and scaled along with 3D primitives. The Z component of translation and scaling is ignored. The X and Y components would be interpreted as U and V values because they apply to the space in which profiles are defined.
Example - Mapping a Texture Inside a Sphere
There are many uses for the  Primitive   SOP . Normally, if you apply a texture onto a sphere, it is mapped onto the outside surface because the U surface normals point outwards by default. If you wanted to map the texture onto the inside of the sphere instead, you could simply run the sphere geometry through a  Primitive   SOP , and select Reverse U (i.e. the surface normals) in the Face/Hull page >  Vertex  menu.

parameters.label: Source  Group
parameters.name: group
parameters.description: If there are input groups, specifying a group name in this field will cause this  SOP  to act only upon the group specified. You can specify profile curves within the group by providing a profile pattern (e.g. *.3 specifies the fourth profile in all spline surfaces).

parameters.label: Template  Group
parameters.name: templategrp
parameters.description: A subset of template points to transform to.

parameters.label: Do Transformation
parameters.name: doxform
parameters.description: When checked, allows transformations to occur.

parameters.label: Rotate to Template
parameters.name: dorot
parameters.description: ⊞  - A template can be specified using the second input of the  Primitive   SOP . When set to On, this template can be used to transform each primitive to the location and orientation of the template point. This is similar to what the  Copy SOP  does except that the actual primitives are transformed, not copies made.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't rotate.

parameters.label: On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: The primitive gets rotated as if its normal was (0,0,1), and is meant to point the same direction as the template normal.

parameters.label: Match Normals
parameters.name: match
parameters.description: Rotates the primitive so that its real normal lines up with the normal of the template point.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the overall transform order for the transformations. The transform order determines the order in which transformations take place. Depending on the order, you can achieve different results using the exact same values. Choose the appropriate order from the menu.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the order of the rotations within the overall transform order.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields move the input geometry in the three axes. Profiles use tx and ty only.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields rotate the Source geometry in the three axes. Profiles use rz only.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields scale the Source geometry in the three axes. Profiles use sx and sy only.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - The pivot point for the transformations. Profiles use px and py only.

parameters.label: Lookat  Object
parameters.name: lookat
parameters.description: Selects the object the primitive should point towards. This performs the lookat in object space; if you need to a lookat in world space, use the lookat in the object's Transform page instead.

parameters.label: Up-Vector
parameters.name: upvector
parameters.description: ⊞  - Defines the orientation of the primitive along the X, Y, or Z axes.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.name: doclr
parameters.description: ⊞  - If Keep is selected, the color attribute is left unchanged. If Add is selected, this parameter changes the color of input primitives according to diffuse color field. If No is selected, the color attribute is removed.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.name: diff
parameters.description: ⊞  - The color to add.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: The alpha value to add.

parameters.label: Crease
parameters.name: docrease
parameters.description: ⊞  - If Keep is selected, the crease attribute is left unchanged. If Add is selected, this parameter generates a crease attribute for the primitive. If No is selected, the crease attribute is removed.

parameters.label: Crease
parameters.name: crease
parameters.description: Attribute is used to set edge crease weights for subdivision surfaces (see  Subdivide SOP ). The Crease Weight attribute for a primitive sets all edges of the polygon to the value specified. On shared edges, the maximum of the two crease weights is used to define the sharpness of the subdivided surface. Crease weights should be larger than 0, with larger values defining sharper edges.

parameters.label: Custom Attrib
parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: Sequence of custom attributes to be added to the geometry created.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: attr0name
parameters.description: Creates a custom attribute with this name.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.name: attr0size
parameters.description: ⊞  - The size of the attribute to create. It'll use however many values from the Value parameter as the size is.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: attr0value
parameters.description: ⊞  - The value(s) to assign to the attribute.

parameters.label: Preserve Shape U
parameters.name: pshapeu
parameters.description: These options only become available once a type of clamping or closure has been selected.

parameters.label: Closure
parameters.description: Change the closure and clamping of a face or hull.

parameters.label: Preserve Shape V
parameters.name: pshapev
parameters.description: These options only become available once a type of clamping or closure has been selected.

parameters.label: Closure
parameters.description: Change the closure and clamping of a face or hull. The options are:

parameters.label: Close U
parameters.name: closeu
parameters.description: ⊞  - Close the primitive in U / V. Select from: Open, Closed Straight, Close Rounded, and Unroll. When you unroll a closed curve you duplicate the wrapped points (you make them unique) and turn the curve into an open curve. The shape of the curve does not change. Same goes for hulls, only there we unique entire rows and cols. This addresses a problem with texturing wrapped surfaces whereby the texture repeats itself in the wrapped portion of the surface.

parameters.label: Close V
parameters.name: closev
parameters.description: ⊞  - Close the primitive in U / V. Select from: Open, Closed Straight, Close Rounded, and Unroll. When you unroll a closed curve you duplicate the wrapped points (you make them unique) and turn the curve into an open curve. The shape of the curve does not change. Same goes for hulls, only there we unique entire rows and cols. This addresses a problem with texturing wrapped surfaces whereby the texture repeats itself in the wrapped portion of the surface.

parameters.label: Clamp U
parameters.name: clampu
parameters.description: ⊞  - Clamp the primitive in U / V. Select from: Clamp, Unclamp.

parameters.label: Clamp V
parameters.name: clampv
parameters.description: ⊞  - Clamp the primitive in U / V. Select from: Clamp, Unclamp.

parameters.label: Vertex
parameters.name: vtxsort
parameters.description: ⊞  - Reorder the vertices in a number of ways.

parameters.label: No change
parameters.name: samevertex
parameters.description: Does not affect the ordering of the vertices.

parameters.label: Reverse
parameters.name: reverse
parameters.description: Reverses both U and V for hulls, and just U for faces.

parameters.label: Reverse U
parameters.name: reverseu
parameters.description: Reverses column order of hulls.

parameters.label: Reverse V
parameters.name: reversev
parameters.description: Reverses row order of hulls.

parameters.label: Swap U and V
parameters.name: swapuv
parameters.description: Interchanges rows/columns while preserving topology.

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.name: shift
parameters.description: Cycles the vertices by "U Offset" and "V Offset".

parameters.label: U Offset
parameters.name: vtxuoff
parameters.description: Cycles face or hull columns / rows when the Shift operation is selected.

parameters.label: V Offset
parameters.name: vtxvoff
parameters.description: Cycles face or hull columns / rows when the Shift operation is selected.

parameters.label: Meta-Surface Weight
parameters.name: metaweight
parameters.description: When selected, allows meta-surface weighting.

parameters.label: Weight
parameters.name: doweight
parameters.description: Enter weight of meta-surface here when Meta-surface Weight is selected.

parameters.label: Particle Render Type
parameters.name: doprender
parameters.description: When On the Particle Type menu below allows section of particle render type.

parameters.label: Particle Type
parameters.name: prtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects how the particles are rendered.

parameters.label: Render as Lines
parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: Each particle will be rendered as a 2-point line, with the length determined based on the particles velocity. If the particle has no velocity it will just be a single pixel in size.

parameters.label: Render as Point Sprites
parameters.name: pointprites
parameters.description: For use with the  Point Sprite MAT . Each particle is a square of pixels that always face the camera. The size of the square is determined by parameters in the Point Sprite and the  pscale  vertex/point attribute. The point sprites will have texture coordinates generated for them automatically also ((0,0) in the bottom left and (1,1) in the top right).

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

n explores Point Operators (POPs), a new GPU-accelerated operator family in TouchDesigner, to prepare for an informative workshop. POPs create and modify 3D data, replacing the older SOPs (Surface Operators) with enhanced performance and flexibility. ## 1. What are POPs? - **Definition**: POPs (Point Operators) are a family of operators in TouchDesigner that run on the GPU, leveraging high parallelism to create and manipulate 3D data efficiently. - **Purpose**: They generate and modify points, primitives, and attributes for rendering (via Render TOP) or output to external devices like LED arrays or lasers. - **Significance**: POPs replace SOPs with GPU acceleration, memory optimization, and integration with modern workflows (e.g., USD, FBX). ## 2.
